teaser.text: Delta Air Lines sells different versions of the same basic product: a journey by air. It also sells cargo space, holiday packages and aviation expertise.

stock.title: Delta stock forecast
stock.meta_description: Delta's weighted scenario reaches $109.40 by October 2029 as premium and loyalty revenue must outlast fuel and fleet pressure.
stock.opening: Delta's weighted scenario reaches $109.40 by October 2029, with the bear case at 28% probability, the base case at 52%, and the bull case at 20%. It hinges on turning premium and loyalty strength into a durable TRASM-over-CASM-ex spread before fuel and fleet obligations catch up.
stock.closing: The full memo also explains Delta's business, rivals, management and risks.

blocks.heading: Where could Delta's shares be by October 2029?

paragraphs.text: The forecast puts the weighted price at $85.47 in October 2027, a 13% return including dividends. It reaches $109.40 in October 2029, a 47% return including dividends. The bear case carries 28% probability, versus 52% for the base case. The bull case carries 20%.

blocks.heading: What has to go right for Delta's base case, and what could go wrong?

paragraphs.text: Operating profit is the central earnings assumption. The base case rises from $6,650 million in October 2027 to $7,008 million in October 2028. It reaches $7,372 million in 2029. The first figure assumes $70,000 million of revenue and a 9.5% margin, supported by premium revenue growing faster than premium seats and by 20% fourth-quarter revenue guidance on seat growth capped at 2%.

The bear case starts at $4,515 million and reaches $4,824 million in 2028. It reaches $5,213 million in 2029 because fuel, labor and disruption costs initially overwhelm fare recovery. The bull case starts at $7,403 million and reaches $8,475 million in 2028. It reaches $9,480 million if fuel normalizes, capacity remains disciplined and premium pricing holds. The base also sits above the $5,250 million 2022–2025 operating-income average, but below an aggressive margin recovery.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Delta really make?

paragraphs.text: Delta’s own free-cash-flow measure was $4,643 million in 2025. It adjusts the starting cash-flow figures for items such as pension funding, selected airport projects and strategic investments. Stock compensation was $313 million. Subtracting it gives an analytical “real” free cash flow of $3,530 million. The annual dividend was $440 million.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay today for Delta?

paragraphs.text: Delta Air Lines is priced as if a capital-hungry airline can turn volatile demand and fuel costs into dependable earnings and cash. The central question is what that price already assumes.

dividend.opening: Delta pays a quarterly dividend of $0.215 per share, and its annual dividend was $440 million. Delta's real free cash flow was $3,530 million, covering that annual dividend.
dividend.closing: The full Delta analysis also explains its business, rivals, management and risks.

blocks.heading: How much does Delta pay in dividends?

paragraphs.text: Shareholder returns resumed gradually. Delta restarted dividends after the pandemic period, while no buybacks occurred in the period. In June 2025, the board authorized a $1 billion repurchase program, but an authorization is only permission to buy shares; it is not money spent. In June 2026, Delta lifted its quarterly dividend to $0.215 per share.

paragraphs.text: The dividend begins at the current annualized $0.86. The base case raises it to $0.90 in 2027 and $1.00 in 2028, before reaching $1.10. The bear case holds it at $0.86 because aircraft spending and weak cash generation could repeat the suspension seen in 2021–22. The bull case reaches $0.98, $1.20 and $1.45 as free cash flow improves.

The December 2026 quarter tests whether fares and unit revenue can keep pace with fuel and non-fuel costs. Delta’s pilot agreement becomes amendable on December 31, 2026; negotiations could affect pay, scheduling and staffing. Recovery depends on fuel easing and TRASM again outpacing non-fuel unit costs in 2027. Airbus deliveries start in 2029 and Boeing deliveries in 2031, requiring a cash bridge before deliveries begin.

blocks.heading: What is Delta's dividend yield today?

paragraphs.text: Investors also track revenue and cost per available seat-mile. An available seat-mile is one seat flown one mile, whether occupied or empty; a 100-seat plane creates that capacity as it flies. Revenue per seat-mile must exceed cost per seat-mile across strong and weak periods. Free cash flow is the money left after necessary investment, especially aircraft spending. Delta can use it for debt, aircraft, dividends or buybacks, so a cash-flow yield is not an automatic shareholder payment.

earnings.opening: Delta's next results are expected on January 12, 2027. Watch whether higher fares become durable cash while labor and legal risks remain manageable.
earnings.closing: The full memo also answers questions about Delta’s business, rivals, management and risks.

blocks.heading: What has Delta guided for the year?

paragraphs.text: Management still promises profit, cash generation and lower debt, but fuel has sharply narrowed its margin for error. Delta’s October 9 outlook cut full-year adjusted earnings per share to **$5.10–$5.60**, from **$6.50–$7.50**. Adjusted earnings remove selected unusual items to show recurring performance; they are accounting profit, not cash in the bank.

Free cash flow asks what remains after operations and long-lived investment. Leverage compares debt with an earnings measure. That is why debt can fall while leverage worsens if fuel reduces earnings. Delta’s promises include **$2.5 billion** of free cash flow, **$5 billion** of capital spending and gross leverage of **2.2 times**.

blocks.heading: Did Delta keep its past promises?

paragraphs.text: Promises require a separate test. Adjusted earnings remove specified items from standard profit, while free cash flow is the cash left after running the business and making necessary investments. Delta forecast 2025 adjusted earnings above US$7.35 per share but delivered US$5.82. It later reduced its 2026 free-cash-flow outlook from US$3–4 billion to approximately US$2.5 billion, citing higher fuel costs.

blocks.heading: What do Delta's last eight quarters show?

paragraphs.text: September 2026 showed strong revenue growth but weaker profit retention. Revenue reached $20,186 million. It was $16,673 million in the comparable quarter. Operating income fell to $1,454 million, while net income fell to $756 million.

blocks.heading: What should I watch in Delta's next results?

paragraphs.text: The next evidence will show whether higher fares become durable cash while labor and legal risks remain manageable. The December 2026 quarter should reveal whether realized fuel prices and revenue per unit of capacity move together. Advance bookings provide cash early, but Delta still owes those customers a flight.
